exploration.prompt: Forty minutes before the corridor finds out.

interactables.label: Read it properly
interactables.internal_thought: (No student is named. No school is named except as "a local academy." She's built the whole thing so that nobody can find a seventeen-year-old at the end of it.)
interactables.follow_up: (There's a line in the eleventh paragraph: "A person with knowledge of the review, who is not a public official and who requested anonymity for reasons of immigration status." She put that in on purpose. She's daring somebody to be the one who says it out loud.)

interactables.label: DeepThread
interactables.internal_thought: (Two hundred and eleven users and the board has done four hundred posts in ninety minutes. It's never done forty in a day.)
interactables.follow_up: (The nine are gone. Taki's rota — the nine accounts that always turn up to tell people they're misremembering — haven't posted since 06:04.)

interactables.label: Glimpse
interactables.internal_thought: (Amber Clarke has posted a black square with the caption PRAYING FOR OUR TOWN. It has nine hundred likes and forty comments and eleven of the comments are people who lost somebody in 2013.)
interactables.follow_up: (She's deleted it by seven. She has never deleted anything.)

interactables.label: Riley — 14 missed calls
interactables.internal_thought: (Fourteen between 6:03 and 6:31. Then one message: "my father's name is in paragraph 29".)

interactables.label: Find paragraph 29
interactables.internal_thought: (The seafront redevelopment. "Designed by Jones & Associates, a firm which has since been retained by Cross Industries on four subsequent municipal contracts.")
interactables.follow_up: (That's all it says. It's accurate, it's public record, it's not an accusation of anything. And it's got his name in it, in a statewide paper, next to the word storm.)

interactables.label: The letter, still unopened
interactables.internal_thought: (Twenty-four days.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz

dialogue_sequence.text: Everyone in here is somebody's kid. And this morning about a third of them found out their dad or their mum or their uncle was in a room in 2013 and hasn't mentioned it.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Kieran Ness
dialogue_sequence.text: That's not a scandal. That's two hundred separate breakfasts that went wrong.

choices.choice_text: "You wrote that on your board, didn't you."

dialogue_sequence.text: My dad drove a recovery truck in 2013. Pulled cars off the coast road for nine days.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Kieran Ness
dialogue_sequence.text: This morning he read paragraph six and put his coffee down and said, out loud, to nobody: "we thought they'd been told to go."

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Kieran Ness
dialogue_sequence.text: Eleven years of a man thinking those people made a bad choice. And this morning he found out they made the choice they were told to make and then the telling stopped.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (That's what I've done. Not to Cross. To a man with a recovery truck.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Sandra Johnson
dialogue_sequence.text: That's not a good reason. I know it's not a good reason. It's the actual one.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Zoey Brookes
dialogue_sequence.text: You sat on a floor for Riley Jones and did the shutting-up thing and I have thought about it approximately once a week since.

dialogue_sequence.text: My mother is in paragraph thirty-four.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Zoey Brookes
dialogue_sequence.text: She was the county clerk. She's the one who filed the thirty-eight page version.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Zoey Brookes

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (I don't say anything. I've got about four things and every one of them would be for me and not for her.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Zoey Brookes
dialogue_sequence.text: I'm not asking you to feel bad. Everything in that article is true. I've read it four times and every single fact in it is true.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Zoey Brookes
dialogue_sequence.text: Here's what I want to say and then you can go.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Zoey Brookes
dialogue_sequence.text: I was horrible to Riley Jones for two years and I'm not going to explain it, because explaining it turns into excusing it and I've watched my whole family do that for a decade.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Zoey Brookes
dialogue_sequence.text: I did it because it worked. Because being the one who says the thing means nobody says it about you. That's it. That's the whole architecture.

"I know. I've been doing my own version of it for a year."

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Zoey Brookes

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Zoey Brookes
dialogue_sequence.text: One thing, because you'll find out anyway and I'd rather it came from me.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Luke Pierce
dialogue_sequence.text: I've been Jake Cross's friend since we were six. Six. You don't pick anything at six, you just end up next to somebody.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Luke Pierce
dialogue_sequence.text: And then you're fourteen and he's doing something and you're standing there, and then you're seventeen and you're a Crosshair, which is a name he made up, and I laughed when he made it up because that's what I do.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Luke Pierce
dialogue_sequence.text: I'm not stupid. Everyone thinks I'm stupid. I'm slow, that's not the same, I just need a second and nobody in that group has ever given me a second.

dialogue_sequence.text: (He didn't get the passport joke in October. He said so, out loud, and got called an idiot for it in front of forty people.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (He didn't get it because it wasn't funny. He was the only person in that hallway who reacted correctly.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Luke Pierce
dialogue_sequence.text: There's a thing. From 2013. I've never told anyone and I'm going to tell you badly.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Luke Pierce
dialogue_sequence.text: I was six. We were up at my grandmother's on the ridge, which is why we were fine. And I was at the window.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Luke Pierce
dialogue_sequence.text: And I saw something come down out of the sky into the bay.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Luke Pierce
dialogue_sequence.text: Orange. Really orange. It came down slow and it went sideways at the end and then it was just gone in the water.

dialogue_sequence.text: I told my mum and she said it was the storm and to go to bed. I told Jake when we were about ten and he told everyone I said aliens.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Luke Pierce
dialogue_sequence.text: Seven years, man. Seven years of alien Luke.

dialogue_sequence.text: (That's a marine flare. That is exactly and only a marine flare, and any adult in a coastal town would have known that in about a second and a half.)

dialogue_sequence.text: (Which means somebody was out on that water on the night of the storm, in the dark, firing distress signals. And every adult who heard a six-year-old describe it decided to call it the storm and put him to bed.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Luke Pierce
dialogue_sequence.text: ...A flare.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Luke Pierce
dialogue_sequence.text: Like a — like somebody in trouble.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Luke Pierce
dialogue_sequence.text: I was six and I saw somebody asking for help and I told three grown-ups and every single one of them said storm.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Luke Pierce
dialogue_sequence.text: I'm going to be sick. Sorry. I'm — give me a second.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz

dialogue_sequence.text: Don't.

dialogue_sequence.text: Whatever the smug thing is, don't. I've had a morning.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Amber Clarke
dialogue_sequence.text: Yeah. Because a woman commented saying her son was on the list and thank you for remembering him.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Amber Clarke
dialogue_sequence.text: I didn't remember him. I posted a black square because everyone was posting and I had nothing and a black square is what you post when you've got nothing.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Amber Clarke
dialogue_sequence.text: And she thanked me.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz

dialogue_sequence.text: Nine thousand followers. Do you know what my most-viewed thing is? Ever? Of everything I've made?

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Amber Clarke
dialogue_sequence.text: It's Riley Jones's face in a corridor.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Amber Clarke

dialogue_sequence.text: Make what? I don't — that's the thing nobody gets. I'm not talented. Chase is talented. Maddie's talented.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Amber Clarke
dialogue_sequence.text: I'm loud. That's my entire skill set. I'm loud in a school where being loud is worth something and in about eight months I'm going to be loud in a world where it isn't.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Amber Clarke
dialogue_sequence.text: God. Why am I saying this to you. You're the one person here who's allowed to enjoy it.

dialogue_sequence.text: (I'm not enjoying it. I want to. I've wanted to for two months and now it's here and it's a girl on a floor in a corridor.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (And somewhere behind my eyes something says: she'd have filmed you on this floor. Don't confuse a bad week with a change.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (That one's definitely not me. I know the voice now.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Elise Turner-Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: I'm not upset. I'm thirty-one and I've been in this house four years and I keep waiting to feel something and what I actually feel is quieter.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Elise Turner-Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: Sit down. Both of you. I've made tea nobody wants, it's what I do.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (She's put three cups out. She's put three cups out in a house where nobody comes downstairs.)

dialogue_sequence.text: You asked me a question in November. In this kitchen. You asked if I was happy.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Elise Turner-Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: I've thought about it every day since. Which is embarrassing, because it's four words, and a seventeen-year-old said it.

choices.choice_text: "You don't owe me anything for asking."

dialogue_sequence.text: Three years ago I found a folder on his computer. "Bay Reconstruction — 2013 Confidential."

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Elise Turner-Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: I copied it onto a drive. I don't know why. I've never opened it — I opened one file and it was a spreadsheet and I closed it.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Riley Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: You've had it for three years.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Elise Turner-Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: In a tampon box. Under the sink. Because that is the one place in this house that man was never going to look, and I want you to understand that I chose it on purpose and I have thought about that choice with some pride.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (Riley makes a sound that is not quite a laugh.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Elise Turner-Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: Here's my condition, and it's the only one.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Elise Turner-Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: Theo doesn't get dragged. Whatever's on there, whatever it does to Richard — that boy has been in an upstairs room for eleven years and he is not going to be a paragraph.

choices.choice_text: "I can't promise what other people print."

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Elise Turner-Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: Riley.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Elise Turner-Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: I'm not going to try to be your mother. I've never tried, actually — I've tried to be a person you didn't mind, which is a much smaller job and I've still been bad at it.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Elise Turner-Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: But if you want the house, it's yours and Theo's. I'll go back to Portland. I've got a flat and a client list and I've had them the whole time.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Riley Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: ...Don't.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Riley Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: Don't go yet. Theo needs somebody in the house who isn't me and I've been the somebody since I was six.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (Elise Turner-Jones puts a hand over her mouth in her own kitchen and doesn't say anything for about nine seconds.)

scenes.director_note: First time Gerald is seen. Ordinary office, ordinary man, ordinary sixty-two. Nothing about the room should signal villainy. No score.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (He came out to reception himself. Shook my hand. Asked if I'd found parking, which is an odd thing to ask a boy who walked.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Gerald Cross
dialogue_sequence.text: Sit down, Hafizh. Tea, coffee, water. I'd recommend the water, the machine's terrible.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Gerald Cross
dialogue_sequence.text: I asked you here. I want that established. You didn't come and confront me — I picked up a telephone and asked, and you said yes.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (He's right and I hate that he's right.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Gerald Cross
dialogue_sequence.text: The article's accurate. Every fact in it. I've had four lawyers on it since six this morning and the best they've given me is that paragraph nineteen is unfair in emphasis.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Gerald Cross
dialogue_sequence.text: Unfair in emphasis. Forty thousand pounds a year, that opinion.

choices.choice_text: "Why did you sign the emergency review?"

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Gerald Cross
dialogue_sequence.text: Records.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (No pause. No consideration. He answers a question I have spent two months building toward like I've asked him the time.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Gerald Cross
dialogue_sequence.text: School records, municipal records, insurance files, the contents of a records room that had four feet of seawater in it. Paper, Hafizh. Twenty feet of wet paper.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Gerald Cross
dialogue_sequence.text: In November 2013 this town had no landfill capacity, no incinerator inside eighty miles, and a public health order about mould. My company had a barge.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Gerald Cross
dialogue_sequence.text: It was illegal. Straightforwardly. Marine dumping, and I'd be fined into the ground for it today, and it's eleven years past the statute.

choices.choice_text: "Four hundred yearbooks aren't a public health emergency."

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Gerald Cross
dialogue_sequence.text: One.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Gerald Cross
dialogue_sequence.text: There was one. I paid for one, I watched one go over the side, and I have thought about it approximately every day for eleven years, so I would remember two.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (And there it is. The first thing this man has said today that cost him something.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Gerald Cross
dialogue_sequence.text: Where's the second one.

choices.choice_text: "You'd know if you'd looked. You've never looked."

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Gerald Cross
dialogue_sequence.text: No. I've never looked. I've had eleven years and a survey company and I have never once put a boat over that channel.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Gerald Cross
dialogue_sequence.text: You'll think that's guilt. It isn't. It's that I decided in 2014 that the thing I had done was the smallest available wrong, and I have protected that decision very carefully by never testing it.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Gerald Cross
dialogue_sequence.text: Which is what everybody does. I'm not special, I'm just solvent.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Gerald Cross
dialogue_sequence.text: Now. Why I asked you here.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Gerald Cross
dialogue_sequence.text: The leak didn't come from your files.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (What.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Gerald Cross
dialogue_sequence.text: The Oregonian had the thirty-eight-page discrepancy and the siren timings on Tuesday. You were on a boat on Tuesday. Your journalist filed at eleven on Wednesday night and she'd had the core of it since Monday.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Gerald Cross
dialogue_sequence.text: Somebody else has been feeding that paper for a fortnight. And I'd have assumed it was Brandstone building her own case, except that some of what she was sent isn't real.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Gerald Cross
dialogue_sequence.text: A control-room log. Timestamped, formatted correctly, my company's letterhead. It shows a manual shutdown sequence with a name on it.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Gerald Cross
dialogue_sequence.text: It's a forgery. I know it's a forgery for one reason and it is not a reason I enjoy: that log never existed. Not destroyed. Never made. We were in a room with no power making decisions by torchlight.

dialogue_sequence.text: I've spent all afternoon thinking I was too gullible. I was too careful. I was too careful to be worth forging for.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (She sits down on the floor next to her boxes and puts her hands over her face and I let her have it.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Taki Kimura
dialogue_sequence.text: I'm putting the wall back up.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Taki Kimura
dialogue_sequence.text: Not tonight. But I'm putting it back up, and this time I'm putting a third colour on it for things somebody handed me.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Taki Kimura
dialogue_sequence.text: That's not paranoia. That's just — that's methodology.

scenes.location: Blackwell Academy — Pool hall, empty, 9:00 PM
scenes.director_note: Same hall as ep2_14. Full lights this time, not the underwater bank. It should look wrong.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Riley Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: You picked here.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Riley Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: Whatever this is, you picked the room where I went under. That's either very kind or very calculated and I genuinely can't tell.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (Neither. I picked it because I don't know where else in this building is mine.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (I tell her. All of it, in order, for eleven minutes, and she doesn't interrupt once.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Riley Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: Okay.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Riley Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: I'm going to say three things and I've been assembling them since the word Ezra and I'd like to get through all three.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Riley Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: One. My father's name is in a newspaper in four states and he's in a hotel in Portland and Theo asked me this morning whether we're poor now, and I didn't know.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Riley Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: Two. Mason can't hold four minutes.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Riley Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: Three.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Riley Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: Somebody put a thing on your camera to make you interesting to me.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (That's not what I expected. That's not even close to what I expected.)

choices.choice_text: "That's not what happened. You were before any of it."
"The pool wasn't hers. She said so herself."
"I don't know how to answer that."

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: We were friends in March. You made me sit through a whole film about a horse in April.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: She put the frames on my card in the first week of November. Everything that matters was already there.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Riley Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: ...Okay.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Riley Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: Okay. Sorry. That's — I've had a day where a lot of things turned out to be arranged and I got frightened that we were one.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Riley Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: The horse film was good, by the way. You've never admitted the horse film was good.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (And then she does something I don't expect at all. She takes her shoes off and sits on the edge and puts her feet in.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Riley Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: Don't say anything about it.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Riley Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: I've done it four times since. On my own. That's the thing I was saving to tell you and now it's tonight and it's the wrong night, but there it is.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Riley Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: So what do we do about her.

choices.choice_text: "She's got a dive log with the word FOUND on it."

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Riley Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: Then here's mine, and it's not generous, it's just what I've got.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Riley Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: Her mother's on a stone at the lighthouse and she thinks her father's in a box in the water and she's been alone with it since she was ten.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Riley Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: I have been carrying one thing on my own since I was six and it made me somebody who couldn't get in a bath.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Riley Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: So I understand her completely and she got Mason's skull broken.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Riley Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: That's where I am. That's the whole of where I am and I don't have a fourth thing.

scenes.location: The Calder house. Olivia's room. Nobody in it but the two of them.
scenes.director_note: The Dark Side is genuinely delighted for the first half. That should be more unsettling than any of his previous cruelty. He is also, for the first time, wrong about something — and Fiz catches it.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (Her room. The wall of paper. The box marked MADE, open, forty-one entries.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (And him, on the end of the bed, with his ankles crossed, looking like a man who's won an argument at a dinner party.)
Four episodes.
Four episodes of you telling me people are better than I say. And it turns out the kindest person in the whole town was aiming you like a rifle.
I'm not going to pretend. This is the best night I've had.

choices.choice_text: "You're wrong and I'll show you where."
[Let him have his lap of honour.]

dialogue_sequence.text: Barry Deskowsky turned off a siren and called it a failure for eleven years. Harrison Carter voted for a sale and took an endowment. Gerald Cross dropped a town's paperwork in the sea.
Linda Jacquelin knew about Joyce and said eat your eggs. Marcus Islah watched from a doorway for a couple of seconds first. Elena Ward warned you about your visa and then went and sat on a staircase.
Every single one of them made the small compromise. Every one had a reason. Every one of the reasons was good.
That's my whole case. That's been my case since a diner with rain in it. People are not cruel. People are reasonable, one instalment at a time, until a girl is alone with a dive log for seven years.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (And he's right. He's completely right and I've spent nine weeks confirming it in person, room by room.)
So. Say it. You've been not-saying it since the car park.

choices.choice_text: "You've never once been wrong. Until tonight."

dialogue_sequence.text: Go on then.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: You said the kindest person in town aimed me like a rifle.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: She told me herself she didn't. Word for word: I aimed you, and I did not control one single thing you did after that.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: She could have taken credit. She's the only person in this entire town who had something to gain from lying and she gave the pool back to me.
...That's sentiment.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: It's a fact. You do facts. You've done facts for nine weeks and you've never once let me off with a feeling.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: Your case is that everyone compromises. Fine. Mine is that Alice Carter stayed in the room. Nolan Burgh gave up a key. Elise kept a drive in a tampon box for three years. Barry Deskowsky read page two eleven years late and then asked for it out loud, in front of a witness, on the day he resigned.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: Every one of those cost something and none of them had to happen.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: You're not wrong about the instalments. You're wrong that they're the whole ledger.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (He doesn't say anything. First time in nine weeks.)
Huh.
That's the first argument you've made instead of a flinch.
I'd like it noted that I'm the one who taught you to do that.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (He stands up. And at the door he stops, and for the first time in four episodes he says something without an edge on it at all.)
Open the letter.
That's not a move. I've got nothing in it. Twenty-five days, and you're going to be somebody's evidence by Christmas, and it's from your mother.
Open the letter.

scenes.director_note: Quietest scene in the season. No choices until the very end. Just a boy and an envelope.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (Twenty-five days on the desk. The stamps are beautiful. She always picks the good ones.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (Three pages. Her handwriting, which slopes uphill because she learned to write on unlined paper.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (Page one is the neighbours. Pak Har's roof. The warung on the corner that changed hands and is now worse. Someone's daughter got into a university in Yogyakarta.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (Page two is Bapak's knee, and the rain, and a long paragraph about a cat that has decided to live with them.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (Page three.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: ("You do not have to write back with news. I know you do not have news. Nobody your age has news, they have weather.")

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: ("You have not said anything true in four months. You say fine and busy and the food is okay. I know what fine means because I invented it for my own mother.")

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: ("So I will not ask. I will tell you a thing instead.")

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: ("When you were seven you found a bird in the road and you did not tell anyone for three days. You kept it in a box behind the kitchen and you fed it and it died anyway and you were very calm about it.")

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: ("I found the box. I did not say anything because you did not want me to know, and I have thought about that decision for ten years and I think now it was the wrong one.")

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: ("You should not have had to be calm on your own at seven. So I am telling you now, ten years late: I knew about the bird. I always knew about the bird.")

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: ("Whatever the box is this time, I know about it too.")

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (There's a photograph in the envelope. The kitchen. The same one that's taped inside my wardrobe door, taken this year, with a cat in it.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (I sit on the floor of Room 214 at two in the morning and I make a noise I haven't made in a year and it is not a quiet one.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (Gina Ortiz knocks once, softly, and doesn't come in, and doesn't say anything, and stands outside the door for about four minutes before she goes.)

choices.choice_text: [Not yet. Put it inside the wardrobe door.]

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (It's three in the afternoon in Purwokerto. She picks up on the second ring, which means she was near the phone, which means she has been near the phone for twenty-five days.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Cheryl Brandstone
dialogue_sequence.text: I'll say the professional part first and then the human part, and I'd like you to hold me to the order.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Cheryl Brandstone
dialogue_sequence.text: Professionally: I nearly printed a forged document. I checked it four ways and it passed four ways and the only reason it isn't in a statewide newspaper is that my friend at the Oregonian wanted a fifth.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Cheryl Brandstone
dialogue_sequence.text: Eighteen months of being careful and I got saved by somebody else being more careful. That's going to sit with me.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Cheryl Brandstone
dialogue_sequence.text: Human part: there's a seventeen-year-old girl who thinks her father is in a container in fifty metres of water, and as of this morning there is a resigning police chief who has read page two.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Cheryl Brandstone
dialogue_sequence.text: So there are four things you can do and every one of them costs somebody.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (Sunrise over the ridge. Same light as the channel, same colour, from a different angle.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Riley Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: Say them.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Cheryl Brandstone
dialogue_sequence.text: One. I publish the forgeries. Full second piece: the evidence was manufactured, here's who, here's why. It's a real story and it's arguably the bigger one.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Cheryl Brandstone
dialogue_sequence.text: It also ends her. A minor, named, in four states, forever.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Cheryl Brandstone
dialogue_sequence.text: Two. You give the dive log to Holt and Deskowsky and let them reopen a missing persons case. That's slow, it's official, and it's the only route that ever gets a boat over that channel.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Cheryl Brandstone
dialogue_sequence.text: Three. You bury the forgery entirely. Nobody ever knows. The 2013 story stands on the real evidence, which it does, and Olivia Calder gets to be a girl who lost her parents.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Cheryl Brandstone
dialogue_sequence.text: Four. You give it all to me and let an adult carry it. That's the one I'd advise and it's the one I'd think less of you for taking, and I'm aware that's unfair.

choices.choice_text: "The dive log goes to Holt. That's it. That's the only thing that finds him."
"Publish the forgeries. All of it. No exceptions for people I like."
"Bury it. The real story stands without her in it."
"I'm going to ask her what she wants."

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Cheryl Brandstone
dialogue_sequence.text: ...Right.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Cheryl Brandstone
dialogue_sequence.text: I've been doing this for six years and it did not occur to me to do that.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Riley Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: That's because you're a journalist and he isn't.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (Riley takes my hand on a set of concrete steps at six in the morning. Second time. Nobody counts but me.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (Eleven seconds.)

scenes.location: Arcadia Bay — North channel, first light

dialogue_sequence.speaker: NARRATION
dialogue_sequence.text: [No dialogue. Grey water. A county harbour patrol launch holding position, engine idling.]

dialogue_sequence.speaker: NARRATION
dialogue_sequence.text: [Officer Darren Holt on deck in a coat that isn't warm enough, holding a photocopied page in a plastic sleeve. A dive log. One word in the notes column.]

dialogue_sequence.speaker: NARRATION
dialogue_sequence.text: [He looks over the side at fifty metres of nothing. Then he looks back at the shore.]

dialogue_sequence.speaker: NARRATION
dialogue_sequence.text: [On the cliff above the old dock road, a girl in a black coat, standing exactly where she always stands. Too far away to read.]

dialogue_sequence.speaker: NARRATION
dialogue_sequence.text: [Cut to black. Title card: LIFE IS STRANGE: EXCHANGE — EPISODE 5, LOST AND FOUND]
